facts.statement: Fossils of Saltasaurus were excavated by José Bonaparte, Martín Vince, and Juan C. Leal between 1975 and 1977 at the Estancia El Brete.
facts.quote: The fossils of Saltasaurus were excavated by José Bonaparte, Martín Vince and Juan C. Leal between 1975 and 1977 at the Estancia "El Brete".

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was named and described by Bonaparte and Jaime E. Powell in 1980.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus was named and described by Bonaparte and Jaime E. Powell in 1980.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was the first sauropod genus known to possess armor made of bony plates embedded in its skin.
facts.quote: It was the first genus of sauropod known to possess armour of bony plates embedded in its skin.

facts.statement: Powell estimated the adult length of Saltasaurus at six meters.
facts.quote: Powell estimated the adult length at six metres.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length of Saltasaurus at 8.5 meters and its weight at 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length at 8.5 m and the weight at 2.5 tonnes (2.8 short tons).

facts.statement: Donald Henderson estimated a larger size for Saltasaurus of 12.8 meters long and 6.87 tonnes.
facts.quote: Donald Henderson estimated a larger size of 12.8 m long and 6.87 t.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was herbivorous, like all sauropods.
facts.quote: Like all sauropods, Saltasaurus was herbivorous.

facts.statement: Powell assumed adult Saltasaurus were protected by body armor while juveniles were protected by the herd.
facts.quote: Powell assumed adult individuals were protected against predators by their body armour, while juveniles were protected by the herd as a whole.

facts.statement: The discovery of Saltasaurus in 1975 forced paleontologists to reconsider sauropod defenses due to its crocodile-like armor plates measuring 10 to 12 centimeters in diameter.
facts.quote: When it was first discovered, in 1975, it forced palaeontologists to reconsider some assumptions about sauropods as Saltasaurus possessed crocodile-like armour (osteoderms) 10 to 12 centimetres (4 to 5 in) in diameter.

facts.statement: Female Saltasaurus dug holes with their back feet to lay clutches of about 25 eggs, which they then buried under dirt and vegetation.
facts.quote: Several hundred female saltasaurines dug holes with their back feet, laid eggs in clutches averaging around 25 eggs each, and buried the nests under dirt and vegetation.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus eggs were about 11–12 cm in diameter and contained embryos with skin impressions showing a mosaic armor of small bead-like scales.
facts.quote: The small eggs, about 11–12 cm (4–5 in) in diameter, contained fossilised embryos, complete with skin impressions showing a mosaic armour of small bead-like scales.

facts.statement: Loricosaurus scutatus is a possible synonym of Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Loricosaurus scutatus? von Huene, 1929

facts.statement: Armor plates previously named as Loricosaurus by Friedrich von Huene are now suggested to belong to Saltasaurus rather than an ankylosaurian.
facts.quote: Earlier, armour plates from the area had been named as Loricosaurus by Friedrich von Huene who assumed them to be from an armoured ankylosaurian. It has been suggested these plates were in fact from Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 73 and 66 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 73 y 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was relatively small among sauropods but still huge by human standards, and it had a head similar to that of diplodocids.
facts.quote: Relativamente pequeño entre los saurópodos, aunque aún enorme para los estándares humanos, tenía una cabeza similar a la de los diplodócidos

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was approximately 12 meters long and weighed an estimated 7 tons.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus medía aproximadamente 12 metros de largo, con un peso estimado de 7 toneladas.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus had a small head with spoon-shaped teeth and thin dental crowns similar to those of Diplodocids.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio grande tenía una cabeza pequeña con dientes de forma de cuchara y coronas dentales delgadas, que es similar a las de los Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: The front caudal vertebrae were about twice as wide as they were tall, while the middle tail vertebrae had elongated centers, creating a robust tail that ended in a thin whip-like tip.
facts.quote: Las vértebras caudales delanteras eran aproximadamente dos veces más anchas que altas y las de la parte media de su cola tenían centros alargados, de esta manera era robusta y terminaba en un extremo delgado formando un látigo.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus possessed lateral vertebral depressions called pleurocoels that resembled shallow surface depressions.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus tenía fosas laterales vertebrales, pleurocoelos, que se asemejaban a depresiones superficiales.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus had short and stout limbs with especially short hands and feet.
facts.quote: Las extremidades eran cortas y rechonchas, con manos y pies especialmente cortos.

facts.statement: Unlike other sauropods, the front and hind legs of Saltasaurus were not positioned vertically beneath the body but were slightly splayed outward.
facts.quote: Las patas delanteras y traseras de Saltasaurus y otros titanosáuridos no estaban verticalmente debajo del cuerpo, como ocurre con otros saurópodos, sino que estaban ligeramente dobladas hacia afuera.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus possessed a series of bony plates and nodules along its dorsal region, featuring prominent bony spines.
facts.quote: Poseía una serie de placas y nódulos óseos a lo largo de la región dorsal, con pronunciamientos de púas óseas.

facts.statement: Smaller rounded or pentagonal bonelets about 7 millimeters in diameter formed a continuous armor between the larger plates.
facts.quote: El segundo tipo consta de pequeños huesecillos, redondeados o pentagonales, de unos 7 milímetros de diámetro, que formaban una armadura continua entre las placas.

facts.statement: The discovery of Saltasaurus eggs embedded in nesting grounds suggests gregarious nesting behavior as a protection and survival strategy with high offspring rates.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de huevos de Saltasaurus enmarcados en zonas de anidamiento, ha planteado un comportamiento gregario como medio de protección y estrategia de supervivencia, con una alta tasa de descendientes.

facts.statement: The original discovery was made in the late 1970s and consisted of a group of six incomplete skeletons.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento original se realizó a finales de la década de 1970 en el , y fueron un grupo de 6 esqueletos incompletos.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Balbuena subgroup of the Salta Group within the El Brete Formation.
facts.quote: Fueron encontrados en el subgrupo Balbuena, del grupo Salta de la Formación El Brete.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus fossils were excavated by José Bonaparte, Martín Vince, and Juan C. Leal between 1975 and 1977 at the El Brete estancia.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Saltasaurus fueron excavados por José Bonaparte, Martín Vince y Juan C. Leal entre 1975 y 1977 en la Estancia "El Brete".

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was named and described by Bonaparte and Jaime E. Powell in 1980, with the type species being Saltasaurus loricatus.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus fue nombrado y descrito por Bonaparte y Jaime E. Powell en 1980, la especie tipo es Saltasaurus loricatus.

facts.statement: The generic name Saltasaurus is derived from the province of Salta in northwestern Argentina where the first fossils were recovered.
facts.quote: Su nombre genérico se deriva de la provincia de Salta, la región del noroeste de Argentina donde se recuperaron los primeros fósiles.

facts.statement: The specific name loricatus means "protected by small armored plates" in Latin.
facts.quote: El nombre específico significa "protegido por pequeñas placas blindadas" en latín.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus belongs to the family Saltasauridae, which was previously called Titanosauridae but was redefined with Saltasaurus as the type genus due to inaccuracies in known remains.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus se ubica dentro de la familia de los Saltasauridae, antes llamada titanosauridae pero lo inexacto de los restos conocidos, ha hecho que se lo cambie a Titanosaurus por Saltasaurus como tipo para la familia.

facts.statement: Almost all studies consistently affirm that Saltasaurus is the most derived or one of the most derived titanosaur genera.
facts.quote: prácticamente todos los estudios afirman consistentemente que Saltasaurus es el género de titanosaurio más derivado o uno de los más derivados.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus proved that titanosaurs were the dominant fauna in South America during the Late Cretaceous, contradicting the view that hadrosaurs like Edmontosaurus displaced primitive sauropods globally as they did in Laurasia.
facts.quote: La importancia del Saltasaurus radica que con él se comprobó que la fauna predominante en Sudamérica, eran los titanosáuridos a finales del Cretácico, contradiciendo la visión que los hadrosáuridos, como el abundante Edmontosaurus, más modernos desplazaron a los primitivos sauropódos de todo el mundo como sucedió en Laurasia.

facts.statement: Since bony armor was previously known only in thyreophorans, Saltasaurus demonstrated that massive sauropods did not need additional protection, helping to reclassify armored finds like Titanosaurus from nodosaurids.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, la presencia de la armadura ósea solo era conocida en los tireóforos y con este descubrimiento se comprobó que los saurópodos con su masivo tamaño no necesitaban otra protección; esto ayudó a comprender otros hallazgos, que habían sido colocados dentro de los nodosáurido por la presencia de armadura como el Titanosaurus.

facts.statement: While relationships within Titanosauria remain highly controversial, most studies agree that Saltasaurus is one of the most derived titanosaur genera.
facts.quote: Si bien las relaciones dentro de Titanosauria son muy controvertidas hasta el día de hoy, prácticamente todos los estudios afirman consistentemente que Saltasaurus es el género de titanosaurio más derivado o uno de los más derivados.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was a herbivore, like all sauropods.
facts.quote: Como todos los saurópodos, Saltasaurus era herbívoro.

facts.statement: Powell suggested that Saltasaurus was aquatic.
facts.quote: Powell sugirió que Saltasaurus era acuático.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus possessed armor similar to a crocodile with osteoderms measuring 10 to 12 centimeters in diameter.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus poseía una armadura similar a un cocodrilo con osteodermos de 10 a 12 centímetros de diámetro.

facts.statement: Previously, it was assumed that size alone was sufficient defense for sauropods.
facts.quote: Anteriormente, se suponía que el tamaño por sí solo era una defensa suficiente para los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Since then, paleontologists have investigated the possibility that other sauropods also had armor, such as Laplatasaurus.
facts.quote: Desde entonces, los paleontólogos han investigado la posibilidad de que otros saurópodos también tuvieran armadura, por ejemplo, Laplatasaurus.

facts.statement: Hundreds of female Saltasaurus dug holes with their hind legs, laid eggs in clutches averaging around 25, and buried the nests under ground and vegetation.
facts.quote: Varios cientos de hembras saltasaurinas cavaron agujeros con sus patas traseras, pusieron huevos en nidadas con un promedio de alrededor de 25 huevos cada una y enterraron los nidos bajo tierra y vegetación.

facts.statement: Small eggs, about 11 to 12 centimeters in diameter, contained fossilized embryos with skin impressions showing a mosaic armor of small bead-like scales.
facts.quote: Los huevos pequeños , de unos 11 a 12 centímetros de diámetro , contenían embriones fosilizados, completos con impresiones de piel que muestran una armadura de mosaico de pequeñas escamas en forma de cuentas.

facts.statement: The genus Saltasaurus was named by Bonaparte and Powell in 1980.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Saltasaurus (genus), Bonaparte and Powell 1980

facts.statement: Saltasaurus belongs to the parent group Saltasaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saltasaurini

facts.statement: Saltasaurus is classified in the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Saltasauridae

facts.statement: Saltasaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Saltasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was one of those titanosaurid sauropods that lived about 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus fue uno de esos saurópodos titanosáuridos y vivió hace unos 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: Saltasaurus was graviportal like other sauropods, meaning it could not run because its hind legs had to stay straight during the loading phase of its walking cycle.
facts.quote: Saltasaurus todavía era graviportal como otros saurópodos, lo que significa que no podía correr porque sus patas traseras tenían que mantenerse rectas en la fase de carga de su ciclo de caminar.

facts.statement: Powell assumed that adult individuals were protected from predators by their armor, while juveniles were protected by the herd as a whole.
facts.quote: Powell asumió que los individuos adultos estaban protegidos contra los depredadores por sus corazass, mientras que los juveniles estaban protegidos por la manada en su conjunto.
